semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all integers n with n > 1, for all integers m, and for all real numbers t: (m divided by n is at most t and t is strictly less than (m plus 1) divided by n) if and only if (m is at most n multiplied by t and n multiplied by t is strictly less than (m plus 1)).
witness_dependencies: none (the statement is an equivalence for all n, m, t with no existential witnesses)

payload.statement_nl: Let n be an integer with n > 1, let m be an integer, and let t be a real number. Then the half-open interval condition m / n <= t < (m + 1) / n is equivalent to the scaled inequality m <= n * t < m + 1.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Let n > 1 be an integer, m an integer, and t a real number. Since n > 1, we have n > 0. Therefore multiplication and division by n preserve strict and non-strict inequalities.

First, assume m/n <= t < (m+1)/n. Multiplying every part by the positive number n gives m <= nt < m+1.

Conversely, assume m <= nt < m+1. Dividing every part by the positive number n gives m/n <= t < (m+1)/n.

Thus m/n <= t < (m+1)/n if and only if m <= nt < m+1, as claimed.
result_payload.proof_summary: The equivalence follows immediately by multiplying or dividing the inequalities by n, using that n>1 implies n>0 so the order is preserved.

used_external_facts: Order preservation under multiplication/division by a positive real number
